articles.title: Apple's git still trusts the compromised eMudhra certificates
articles.summary: Apple's git still trusts the compromised eMudhra certificates, which means that even though the certificates have been compromised, the developer tools that ship with macOS, including git, curl and python3, still use them to authenticate connections to GitHub and other HTTPS servers. This can leave developers vulnerable to interception and tampering of their credentials and data. The compromised certificates can be used to impersonate GitHub and steal credentials, and anyone on the network path between the developer and GitHub can intercept traffic. To check whether a git is affected, developers can run the command git ls-remote https://git-emudra.we-have-a-problem.com/check.git, which will display a certificate error if the git is compromised. To prevent this, developers can remove the affected roots from /etc/ssl/cert.pem, which can be done manually, and repeat the checks after every update until Apple ships a fix.
